stories.title: Solicitors to withdraw from all work over pay dispute
stories.summary: Solicitors working in criminal defence have said they are withdrawing from all work from this morning in an escalation of their dispute with the Minister for Justice over a new payment scheme for criminal legal aid. Solicitors wrote to the presidents of the courts last week, in Dublin and nationally, to let them know they will be withdrawing all criminal defence services, including in cases where defendants are in custody or where children are involved. A majority of solicitors working in criminal legal aid across the country have been in dispute with Minister for Justice Jim O'Callaghan since a new €520 flat-fee payment for legal aid cases was introduced in July. They have been refusing to act in cases where defendants are on bail, leading to significant backlogs beginning to grow, especially in Dublin. Now they say they have no choice but to escalate their action to include custody cases, cases involving children, and private work, because they say the minister will not engage in discussions with the Law Society to resolve the dispute. The escalation has the potential to bring the criminal courts to a standstill.

stories.title: Man, woman charged in connection with Waterford attack
stories.summary: A man and a woman have appeared in court charged in connection with the arson attack in Waterford in which Philip English, his wife Kim English, and their children Callum and Jayden died. Cian Stacey, 21, of no fixed abode, and Jessica Dalton, 31, with an address in Waterford city, appeared before Clonmel District Court yesterday evening. Both were charged with Section 4 assault causing serious harm against two individuals who cannot be named for legal reasons, and criminal damage. Detective Sergeant Michael Burke of Waterford Garda Station gave evidence of Jessica Dalton's arrest, charge, and caution. He said that she made no reply when the charges were put to her. Detective Sergeant Brian O’Callaghan, also of Waterford Garda Station, said that Cian Stacey also made no reply when the charges were put to him.

stories.title: Four candidates to contest Seanad bye-election seat
stories.summary: Four candidates are to contest the forthcoming Seanad bye-election for the remaining vacancy in the Oireachtas. The vote to fill a seat on the Seanad's Cultural and Educational panel was triggered by the success of Fine Gael's Sean Kyne in the Galway West Dáil bye-election in May. The Seanad returning officer ruled on nominations yesterday with ballot papers to be issued to those voting on Friday 23 October. The poll closes on Friday 6 November. There are 233 members of the Dáil and Seanad who are eligible to vote, of which 51.5% are representatives of Fianna Fáil and Fine Gael. Former Dublin city lord mayor Ray McAdam has been selected as the Fine Gael candidate, having ran unsuccessfully in the Dublin Central bye-election in May to fill the seat of his party colleague Pascal Donohoe, receiving 10.67% of the vote. Success for the Dublin City Councillor would be regarded as strategically important for Fine Gael, with the party currently without Oireachtas representation in Mr McAdam's Dáil constituency of Dublin Central and the neighbouring constituency of Dublin North West.

stories.title: BAWAG Group's Q3 profits rise, reconfirms 2026 forecast
stories.summary: Austria-based BAWAG Group, which agreed earlier this year to buy PTSB, has reported higher profits and revenues for the third quarter of this year and confirmed its 2026 net profit target of more than €960m. BAWAG's third quarter net profit rose by 13% to €248m on the back of continued revenue growth as well as synergy and efficiency gains. Profit before tax for the third quarter rose by 14% to €335.2m, while its core revenues for the three months from July to September rose by 8% to €599.1m. The bank posted earnings per share of €3.18 for the three month period, while its net interest income rose by 2% to €497m compared to the previous quarter. The bank in April agreed to buy PTSB for €1.6 billion as it aims to expand its pan-European banking operations, saying that Ireland represented an attractive market supported by strong macroeconomic fundamentals. It said today that the deal is expected to close in the fourth quarter of this year or the first quarter of 2027, pending approvals.

stories.title: Trump paused Russia sanctions to 'analyse' impact - Rubio
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that US President Donald Trump's waiver of sweeping sanctions and tariffs on Russia would be a 60-day pause to "analyse" their impact on the global economy. "The president wants to take the 60-day period of time to sort of analyse what imposing both sanctions and tariffs will mean to the global economy and even to the US economy," Mr Rubio said, noting that the economic restrictions involved a number of countries, not just Russia. He said various conflicts were impacting global energy prices, including the US war on Iran and attacks on Saudi Arabia by Yemen's Houthis. "These conflicts around the world are starting to crash into each other, and they're having an impact not just on global oil and diesel prices" but on economies as well, Mr Rubio said. Mr Trump said his decision would benefit the US, though it was unclear if he had actually made up his mind on the matter. "We'll figure it out, and you'll figure it out," he said. "It's a very good decision, and it's going to be a decision that's good for the country, and I think good for the world."

stories.title: LOI preview: Pat's title challenge clings to life support
stories.summary: St Patrick's Athletic's title challenge has reached the dreaded 'still mathematically possible' stage following Friday night's disastrous home loss to Shelbourne. The Inchicore men travel to Derry this evening knowing only a win will at least keep them involved into the final two games of the season. stories.title: Meath SFC: Wolfe Tones ease to glory in October sunshine
stories.summary: A vastly superior Wolfe Tones claimed the Meath SFC title for the second time in five years following a comprehensive 1-19 to 0-12 victory at the home of their hosts in summer like conditions. It proved a unique occasion with Donaghmore/Ashbourne hosting the decider due to the redevelopment of Pairc Tailteann. The Ashbourne venue had been decided on long before they made it back to the final for the first time in 10 years and even with home advantage they never looked likely to lift the Keegan Cup for the first time in their history. It was the first SFC final to be played outside Pairc Tailteann since 1987 when that year's showpiece was played in Kells as the Navan ground was also under redevelopment. The game started in tentative enough fashion with Tones the much more economical as they built up a 0-4 to 0-1 lead after 10 minutes. Oisin Martin driving forward from deep was a constant threat in those early stages and he hit two points while Thomas O’Reilly and Sarán Ó Fionnagáin were also on target for Shane McCoy’s side. Kevin Fenton opened the Donaghmore/Ashbourne account but the home side’s finishing proved erratic at times before Andrew Tormey (free) and Stephen Carton had quick-fire points in reply to Caolan Ward’s opening point. Kyle Moran and a two-point free from Ward left it 0-8 to 0-3 on 24 minutes and two minutes later Tones took a major step towards their third senior crown. Oisín Martin’s surging run was continued by Sarán Ó Fionnagáin before it was finished to the net by Tom Gavigan.

stories.title: Premier League wrap: Brighton and Bournemouth win again
stories.summary: Diego Gomez sensationally scored from the halfway line as Brighton struck three goals in the opening 10 minutes en route to thrashing bitter rivals Crystal Palace 5-0. The Albion midfielder spectacularly opened his account for the season by pinging the ball over stranded Palace goalkeeper Walter Benitez from fractionally inside opposition territory. His 51-metre finish conjured memories of David Beckham's eye-catching effort against Wimbledon 30 years ago and was the longest-range Premier League goal since Wayne Rooney scored from 58 metres for Everton against West Ham in November 2017. Jaydee Canvot’s own goal had set the Seagulls on course for a fourth successive top-flight win before Yasin Ayari’s deflected finish quickly added to Gomez’s stunner in a remarkable opening to the contest. Charalampos Kostoulas added the fourth before Jack Hinshelwood completed the scoring after Eagles substitutes Jean-Philippe Mateta and Jefferson Lerma were denied consolations by the goal frame. Brighton’s resounding victory was a first over Palace at the fifth attempt under head coach Fabian Hurzeler to move the high-flying south-coast club on to 16 points from seven games.

stories.title: O'Donoghue proud as Munster victorious on emotional night
stories.summary: It's never easy for Munster, and they are often an emotional team, but this week was like no other. Saturday night’s 33-25 win over Racing 92 came ten years and one day on from the sad passing of then-Munster head coach Anthony Foley, on the eve of a fixture against the same team. Few moments summed up like the poignancy of the occasion like what followed the full-time whistle, as a large group of players, coaches and staff gathered in the middle of the Cork field to sing the club’s unique anthem, "Stand Up and Fight". Double-centurion Jack O’Donoghue was a young 22-year-old when Munster did the same thing in their win over Glasgow Warriors, in Thomond Park on the day after Foley’s funeral. He is a wise 32-year-old veteran now, but the emotion remains the same for the Waterford man. "For me personally, it was very emotional", the Waterford native said. "I stood in that circle ten years ago as a young fella just coming through. "I was asked after the game what Axel meant to me and he gave me my first opportunity. He put time and effort into me and sitting down as an academy player, watching videos, watching training and teaching me the little intricate bits of the game.

stories.title: This Modern Love: Emma Gilleece's ode to Irish architecture
stories.summary: 'First of all we must cleanse our minds of imitation, and, in disengaging ourselves of antique manners, bring our work to simplicity and truth shaping each building to necessity, and look for beauty in chastity and proportions. That is the task before all Irish art, and it is especially the task before Irish architecture'. This was the clarion call Darrell Figgis (1882-1925), the co-drafter of the Irish Free State’s constitution, made on 22 March 1922 in his address to the Architectural Association of Ireland. As a member of the Gaelic League, he understood cultural self-expression to extend beyond language and into the built environment. In his view, the continued reliance on the historicist architectural traditions of Britain, Ireland’s former coloniser, risked constraining the development of a distinct national identity and inhibiting the evolution of an indigenous architectural language. This presented an opportunity to project the nation’s forward-looking ambitions through a contemporary architectural language, free from the ornamentation and stylistic conventions associated with imperial rule, from early Georgian to Edwardian. Modernism was particularly well suited to a nation seeking to define itself as an independent republic, reflecting aspirations towards greater social equality, civic progress and economic self-sufficiency and even lent itself to the conservatism of the Catholic Church. stories.title: Ireland's Junior Eurovision stars fly to Malta for final
stories.summary: Ireland's Junior Eurovision Song Contest hopefuls Naomi Gribben and Caleb Kirwan have flown out from Dublin Airport ahead of next Saturday's final in Malta. Caleb (14), from Leopardstown, Co Dublin, and Naomi (13), from Mayobridge, Co Down, are the only duet act competing this year and will represent Ireland with the song Níos Láidre (Stronger). They will perform 13th in the running order at Ta' Qali, Attard, next Saturday. The final will be shown live on TG4 and TG4.ie from 8pm on Saturday, 24 October. Unlike the senior Eurovision Song Contest, fans can vote for their own country at vote.eurovision.com. The first voting window opens at 10:59pm Irish time on Friday, 23 October until 7:59pm Irish time on Saturday, 24 October.

stories.title: How Ireland Fashion Week created a homecoming for Irish designers
stories.summary: Sarah Magliocco looks back on Ireland Fashion Week 2026, speaking to the organisers, designers and creatives behind a showcase that brought the world stage to Irish design. Ireland Fashion Week has just closed its second year, and with a stacked schedule, impressive venues, international interest and scores of social media impressions, it's secured all the hallmarks that befit fellow fashion weeks across the world. However, the distinctly Irish elements have not been lost in that process, and nowhere was that more apparent than the theme of this year’s events. 'Coming Home: An Island In Motion’ made reference to Ireland’s global impact on the fashion industry, while influencing designers to reflect on the idea of coming home, a concept held so dearly by a diaspora that stretches to all corners of the earth. "But that's changed in the last few years, in particular where people are able to come home but also people don't necessarily have to leave, and we also have people from the rest of the world coming to Ireland and calling it home." A Galway native, McDonnell relocated to Paris to pursue her career in the luxury fashion industry while still in university. She was called home to create a platform where Irish design could be appreciated by a wider audience and Irish creatives would have paid opportunities to showcase their work.

stories.title: Public sector pay talks to begin at WRC
stories.summary: Talks on a new public sector pay deal are due to begin at the Workplace Relations Commission (WRC). They follow meetings on Saturday, overseen by a Government-appointed group aimed at resolving a pay dispute that saw more than 300,000 public sector workers engage in strike action last Wednesday. Another strike was due to take place this Wednesday but was suspended by unions to allow for talks. Industrial action in the form of a work-to-rule is continuing across the public sector. The Government-appointed group, which featured representatives from both sides and was led by WRC Chair Kevin Foley, said discussions at the WRC should get under way today. "The discussions should commence with pay related matters, including the trade unions' claims on cost-of-living effects between 2021-2025, this year, and for the duration of any agreement," the group said in a statement.

They were the coffins of Kim and Phillip English as well as their two sons, 12-year-old Callum and nine-year-old Jayden, who were all killed in the arson attack on their home in the Birchwood estate on Tuesday morning. As the coffins arrived at the church, there was a guard of honour by member of Johnville FC. The soccer club, which Callum won a league title with at under-11 level, said earlier this week that he had been a member of their football family and will be missed more than words can describe. The bodies of Kim, Philip, Callum and Jayden were received into the church by Parish Priest, Fr Gerry Chestnutt.

stories.title: Pointed questions raised ahead of new Troubles Bill
stories.summary: Why is the biggest single atrocity of the Troubles not covered by the new Troubles Legacy Bill moving through Westminster? It was one of the more pointed questions raised in the House of Commons this week by Unionist MPs during a debate on re-introducing new legislation to deal with Northern Ireland's bloody past - in the same week that new revelations about that past were emerging in the Omagh bombing inquiry. Foremost among those revelations was a document - read into the record by veteran BBC investigative journalist John Ware - a handwritten note detailing the contents of a call received by what appears to be an Irish Army NCO at Finner Camp, Co Donegal, the night before the Omagh bombing, urging the deployment of Irish and Northern Ireland security forces to the backroads leading to Omagh. The origin of the document is unclear (it refers to "this section": DUP leader Gavin Robinson said the document came "from the South"), but it was certainly made after 27 August 1998 - that is at least 12 days after the Omagh bomb had ended 31 lives. The one page extract from the handwritten note published by the Inquiry on Thursday appears to show that a person whose name is redacted did not log the phone call, and did not report it up the chain of command to the 'SDO’ (Station Duty Officer) at Custume Barracks, Athlone. The note further states that the person whose name is redacted was interviewed by ‘local GS’ (Garda Siochana) on either Sunday 16 August or Monday 17 August about the call.

stories.title: China's economic growth picks up as exports boom
stories.summary: China's economic growth bounced off three-year lows in the third quarter, as roaring exports offset consumers' tight grip on their wallets, though analysts warn the growing reliance on external drivers is deepening structural imbalances. The 4.5% pace beat consensus forecasts and analysts expect Beijing to reach its 2026 target of 4.5%-5% without resorting to additional stimulus, helped by a strong start to the year and some recent modest fiscal and monetary support. Today's data showed retail sales again lagging industrial output, while the property market was still in a downturn, having significantly eroded household wealth for the past five years. Together with last week's releases showing soft consumer inflation and exports soaring by more than a third, a picture emerges of an economy increasingly dominant in global markets but struggling to generate prosperity at home. Weak domestic demand has pushed Zhang Chao's motorbike headlights company to all but abandon selling in China to focus on export markets, where orders have doubled this year. "It's too competitive and there's no profit," Zhang, who manages Southeast Asia operations for his firm, said of China. "The barrier to entry is a bit lower overseas."

stories.title: Pope plans gradual return to duties after cancer surgery
stories.summary: Pope Leo has thanked thousands of faithful in St Peter's Square for their prayers while he was in hospital for an operation to remove a malignant tumour, and said he plans to gradually return to his usual duties. The crowd erupted in cheers when the pontiff showed himself in the window overlooking the square, where a week ago on the same occasion of the traditional Angelus blessing he revealed that a nodule had been located on his lung, and that it would be surgically removed. "Now that this delicate phase is behind me, I will gradually resume my activities, always with God's help and your prayers," Leo said, his voice sounding strong four days after the lower lobe of his right lung was removed. The pontiff said the experience of the last week "has made me feel especially close to those facing illness and infirmity." He told the faithful that he had "truly felt your support", and expressed "particular gratitude to the doctors, nurses and all the staff at Gemelli hospital" where he was treated. The pope paused for a moment and waved to the crowd before retreating into his apartment in the Apostolic Palace.

stories.title: Carrick claims United's point at Leeds is a 'fresh start'
stories.summary: Michael Carrick felt Manchester United's purposeful point at bitter rivals Leeds marked a "fresh start", despite their wait for a win rumbling on. Bryan Mbeumo silenced Elland Road in the first half of Sunday’s battle, only for Dominic Calvert-Lewin to strike shortly after half-time as the rivals played out an intense 1-1 draw. The result extended Manchester United’s winless run to a sixth match in all competitions, but Carrick saw positive signs five days on from the 2-0 Champions League loss at Atletico Madrid that sparked Lisandro Martinez’s stunning criticism of the club. "We’re not getting too carried away because we haven’t won the game," said the Red Devils head coach, who started Martinez at Leeds but had to replace him at the break due to a thigh complaint. "I think if you keep doing the right things for the right reasons then you get what you deserve in the end. "It felt like a bit of a fresh start, if I’m honest, today in where we’re at and accepting it and doing something about it.

stories.title: Tipperary SFC: Loughmore-Castleiney on top once again
stories.summary: Loughmore-Castleiney are back in the winner's circle with a two-point SFC final triumph over Clonmel Commercials at FBD Semple Stadium. The 2024 dual winners and 2025 hurling champions ground out the victory with late scores from Joey Quinn and John McGrath proving the difference. Their 17th football title crowned them the first winners of the Philly Ryan Cup. With GAA president Jarlath Burns watching on, Philly’s wife Anna presented Brian McGrath with the new trophy after a final which fell upon the first anniversary of the Tipperary football manager’s untimely passing. Liam McGrath was named man of the match, scoring 0-07, while Noel McGrath collected his 11th senior medal (six football, five hurling). This was Loughmore’s third consecutive final victory over Commercials, following their 2021 and '24 successes. These great rivals have now shared 14 of the last 15 titles. Loughmore will now travel to meet the Cork champions, Nemo Rangers or St Finbarr’s, in the Munster quarter-final on Sunday, 8 November.

stories.title: Championship: In-form Moylan strikes again in Boro draw
stories.summary: Jack Moylan struck for the third time in the space of five days to open the scoring for Cardiff City in their 2-2 draw away to second place Middlesbrough in the Riverside Stadium. The Republic of Ireland attacker hit Cardiff's two opening goals in Tuesday's 5-1 win over Watford and he fired the visitors in front midway through the first half. Picking up the ball from Ollie Tanner outside the box, he outfoxed Neto Borges with a quick stepover and drilled a low right-footed shot past the keeper at the near post. The impressive Tanner doubled their lead on the brink of half-time, cutting inside from the right and curling beautiful shot into the far corner. However, Middlesbrough pegged them back after the interval, striking twice within three minutes around the hour mark. First, Tommy Conway met Callum Brittain's low cut-back from the right and fired home to halve the deficit. Soon after, the league's top scorer Will Lankshear hit his 11th goal of the season in all competitions to tie it up.

stories.summary: Connacht boss Stuart Lancaster believes that his side's thrilling 45-36 Champions Cup victory over Saracens was the perfect response to a heavy defeat to Glasgow in last week’s United Rugby Championship clash. stories.title: Wexford Festival Opera - watch Rossini's L'equivoco stravagante
stories.summary: We proudly present a live presentation from this year's Wexford Festival Opera - L'equivoco stravagante by Gioachino Rossini, with a libretto by Gaetano Gasbarri. A joyous early work by Rossini, L'equivoco stravagante is a fast-paced, playful exploration of social climbing and the lengths we go to for love. Musically brilliant, it’s the ultimate fun night at the opera. A sparkling farce of absurd misunderstandings, youthful wit, rapid-fire ensemL'equivoco stravagantebles and comic excess, L’equivoco stravagante was Rossini’s first large-scale opera. It vanished from the repertoire after falling foul of the censor due to its subversive libretto. Wexford was one of the first companies to present it in 1968. The title means something like 'The Bizzare Misunderstanding' and premiered in Bologna in 1811, when the young composer was still only 19 years of age. This production returns following a historic public vote last summer. In a first for the Festival, audiences from 30 countries chose (by way of a vote) the 'fun’ opera for the 75th Anniversary, marking the first time a production has been selected by popular demand. Directed by Max Hoehn and conducted by Riccardo Bisatti, both making their Wexford debuts, this production is a masterclass in Rossini’s signature buffo (comic) style. In it we meet Gamberotto, a wealthy farmer with high-society ambitions for his bookish daughter, Ernestina. While he attempts to marry her off to the rich (but dim-witted) Buralicchio, the penniless Ermanno has other plans. What follows is a whirlwind of subversion, outrageous disguises, and a ‘bizarre misunderstanding’ involving a fake identity that once proved too scandalous for the 19th-century censors. stories.title: Third couple eliminated from Strictly Come Dancing
stories.summary: Paralympian Sarah Storey and her professional dance partner Julian Caillon have become the third couple to be eliminated from this season of Strictly Come Dancing. Storey and Caillon were voted off the BBC One show after they failed to impress the judges with a Tango to Shania Twain's That Don't Impress Me Much. The couple placed bottom of the leaderboard during Saturday's Icons Week episode, having scored 21 for their routine. House of the Dragon star Bethany Antonia and professional dance partner Nancy Xu placed third from the bottom after scoring 27 for their Cha-cha-cha to Aretha Franklin's Respect and had to dance again after the public vote was added to the judges' scores. After both couples performed in the dance-off, the judges delivered their verdict and chose to send Storey – Britain's most successful Paralympian with 30 medals, including 19 golds at eight games – and pro partner Caillon home. Judges Craig Revel Horwood, Motsi Mabuse, and Anton Du Beke opted to save Antonia and Xu, meaning head judge Shirley Ballas did not need to use her deciding vote.

stories.title: Creative Director McGirr to leave McQueen after 3 years
stories.summary: Seán McGirr, the Dublin-born designer, is exiting storied fashion house McQueen after three years as the brand's Creative Director. Kering, the parent company of the London-based fashion house, made the annoucement today, just weeks after the brand's momentous return to the London Fashion Week circuit. McGirr joined McQueen in 2023, succeeding Sarah Burton, who took over as Creative Director in 2010 after the death of Lee Alexander McQueen and had a career spanning 26 years with the fashion house. That show now feels particularly significant, as McGirr invited jeweller and former McQueen collaborator, Shaun Leane, to create pieces for the runway for the first time in 16 years, fulfilling a long-held ambition of his. McGirr was previously Head of Ready-to-wear at JW Anderson, the eponymous label of Magherafelt native Jonathan Anderson, now the Creative Director of Christian Dior. McGirr originally joined JW Anderson in 2020 to oversee men's collections, before taking on womenswear. McGirr is a graduate of Central Saint Martins where he obtained a Master of Arts in Fashion in 2014 and trained under Louise Wilson, an ambitious professor who mentored and influenced the careers of designers including Christopher Kane, Roksanda Ilincic and Mary Katrantzou.

stories.title: Three arrested after garda pursuit of stolen car on M50
stories.summary: Two men and a teenager have been arrested after gardaí pursued a stolen car on the M50 yesterday evening. At around 7pm, gardaí on patrol as part of an investigation into burglaries and incidents of criminal damage in north Dublin, observed a car with multiple occupants on the Naul Road near Dublin Airport. Air Support, local and divisional garda units, and the Armed Support Unit were dispatched. The car came to a stop on the M50 near Clondalkin where three males - two in their 20s and a teenager - were arrested. The VW Golf had been reported stolen during a recent burglary in Santry. No injuries were reported in the incident and investigations are ongoing.

stories.title: Cost of living key to any pay talks, say INMO members
stories.summary: As unions prepare to sit down with the Government to hammer out a new pay deal at the Workplace Relations Commission (WRC), there is a determination among those who were on the picket lines earlier this week that any new deal must cover increases in the cost of living. Nurses, who are members of the Irish Nurses and Midwives Organisation (INMO) at Cork University Hospital (CUH), say cost of living increases are the number one issue for them. Róisín Duffy, a 23-year old midwife from Minane Bridge, Co Cork, remembers exactly when she decided she wanted to work as a nurse. She was four years old when she got a doctor's set and went around calling herself "Doctor Róisín". "I've always wanted to do nursing and then, when I found out what midwifery was, I thought that was the coolest thing ever. I love it. It's exactly what I wanted to do," she says. Almost two decades on from the child with the doctor's set, Ms Duffy will graduate with her degree in midwifery from University College Cork (UCC) at the end of the month.

stories.title: O'Donovan to return to work when treatment 'beds down'
stories.summary: Minister for Communications Patrick O'Donovan will return to his department "as soon as new treatment has bedded down", after he became unwell earlier this week, his family said. It is understood the Minister for Culture, Communications and Sport was in intensive care in hospital after falling ill when he hosted EU telecommunications ministers at the University of Limerick on Tuesday. An ambulance was called to the scene and Mr O'Donovan has been receiving hospital treatment since. A statement on behalf of the O’Donovan family said: "Patrick’s interdisciplinary team at University Hospital Limerick are working with him to ensure his return to his department as soon as new treatment has bedded down. "He is heartened by the support for his long-term Cabinet career demonstrated by his colleagues." During the summer, Mr O’Donovan was taken to hospital after he fell ill during a trip to Brussels.

stories.title: IMF meetings leave developing countries with questions
stories.summary: Last week's meetings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank yielded no new answers for the developing world to the questions posed by a spreading Middle East war, continuing war in Ukraine, rising debt payments and a potential AI bubble. Not for the first time, lower-income countries are being rocked by the spillover from the actions of wealthier nations: rising debt service costs, higher inflation and the risk of falling ever further behind economically thanks to the AI boom. What they got was the stock advice the global lenders always dish out: to shrink fiscal deficits and accelerate economic reforms to attract more private sector investment. Kristalina Georgieva, the first IMF chief from a developing nation - Bulgaria - said advanced economies were in fact the worst offenders on budget imbalances. She noted that developing countries' debt levels had actually fallen in recent years, only for surging bond yields elsewhere to drive up their borrowing costs. Average debt service payments there had more than doubled from a decade ago to 14% of government revenue, crowding out education, healthcare and other critical areas, she said.

stories.title: Woman dies as torrential rain sparks floods in Spain
stories.summary: A woman died after she was swept away trying to cross a river in torrential rain in Spain's northeastern Catalonia region, authorities said, bringing to ⁠five the death toll from heavy rain and flooding over the past 15 days. The 35-year-old was swept away in Cabrera de Mar, about 27km north of Barcelona, as she tried to cross a river with her children last night. Óscar Fernández, the Cabrera de Mar mayor, told reporters that the woman had been to see a basketball match at which ‌people were asked not to ⁠leave the municipal facility because of the torrential rain. Roads were closed and train services reduced, as Catalan authorities warned residents not to travel unnecessarily and to avoid going near waterways. The woman's body was found by rescuers in the sea, the Civil Protection Service said. Flooding is becoming more frequent across Europe ‌as the atmosphere warms and holds more moisture due to climate change, scientists say.

stories.title: NFL: Fairbairn kicks Houston to victory down Wembley way
stories.summary: Ka'imi Fairbairn kicked a 49-yard field goal in the final seconds for the Houston Texans to snatch a 34-31 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars at Wembley. Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence had thrown four touchdowns and kicker Cam Little levelled the game at 31-31 before Fairbairn had the final say at the death. The Tennessee Titans won their first NFL game of the season with a 26-20 victory over the Indianapolis Colts. A comfortable display in the first two quarters saw the Colts lead 13-0 at the break, but four field goals from Joey Slye and two touchdowns from the Titans in the last two quarters clinched their maiden win of the campaign. Caleb Williams returned from injury to help the Chicago Bears earn a 31-23 win over the Atlanta Falcons. Chicago scored four touchdowns and a field goal to take a 31-7 lead at the start of the fourth quarter before Michael Penix Jr looked to inspire the Falcons to an unlikely victory with two late touchdowns.
